chunks: My father (rah) said: It was narrated to me by Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ismail ibn Mazar from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Any man from our Shias to whom a man from our brothers comes and seeks his help in a need, and he does not help him while he has the capacity, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will test him by making him fulfill the needs of an enemy from our enemies; Allah will punish him for it on the Day of Resurrection.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence for a Shia who fails to help a brother in need when capable?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith emphasizes the spiritual gravity of *ta'awun* (mutual assistance) within the Shia community, framing neglect not merely as a social lapse but as a divine test. The specific consequence—paying the needs of an enemy—serves as a poetic justice, illustrating how the failure to support one's own 'brothers' in faith results in being compelled to serve their adversaries, thereby incurring punishment on the Day of Judgment.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Ali b. Ibrahim from his father from Ismail b. Mazar from Yunis b. Abdulrahman from Ibn Muskan from Abi Basir from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

If a Shia goes to his brother and seeks help from him in any matter and if the latter has capacity to help him out but does not do so, the Almighty Allah will give him power to help our enemies. He will be punished on the Day of Judgment for doing so.”
